result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both pages use a dark tinted base (navy in A, green-black in B) with a warm cream lower section, which feels deliberate and avoids the usual leaf-green-on-white look. Both also overuse their accents: A puts its coral on the button, a background orb and a whole card, and B puts its yellow on the logo dot, badge, headline word and button. Both tell the cards apart with three loud full-bleed colors (mint/coral/gold in A, mint/lime/tan in B), so neither has a clear overall edge. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both use a dark sea-toned hero over a warm cream section, so neither looks like the usual green-on-white health food site. A sticks to one yellow accent (logo dot, badge, headline word, button), while B spreads its accent across gold text, a coral button, a coral orb and a coral card, so two colors compete. Both tell the product cards apart with three loud fills (A: mint, lime and tan; B: mint, coral and gold). B's card text reads more clearly in the screenshot, but A's tighter accent control gives it the edge.
